description: The agent's vocabulary for AUTHORING neural-network code. Same shape as design_patterns: Concept nodes (the parts), DesignPattern nodes (the recipes), CodeTarget nodes (the workloads where an NN-shaped solution is appropriate). When the code-writing cortex picks a pattern for an NN-shaped target (fuzzy_classification, function_approximation, sequence_relation, embedding_lookup) it ranks these by tag match + expected_speedup just like any other pattern — no NN-specific selection logic. Adding NN building blocks = editing this file.
category_inheritance: genlMt → compiler_theory (cost/equivalence vocabulary) and → code_authoring (target/draft/install workflow). NN authoring sits AT THE SAME LEVEL as compiler-style optimization: both are 'pick a recipe for a workload'.

concepts.name: tensor
concepts.definition: Typed N-dimensional array of numeric values. The substrate of every NN computation; weights, activations, gradients are all tensors of various shapes.

concepts.name: weight
concepts.definition: A learnable scalar parameter inside a layer. Updated each training step by the optimizer toward lower loss. Persistent across forward passes.

concepts.name: bias
concepts.definition: A learnable additive scalar per output unit. Lets a layer represent functions that don't pass through the origin.

concepts.name: activation
concepts.definition: The output tensor of a layer. Carries the information that the next layer will transform.

concepts.name: layer
concepts.definition: A parametric tensor transformation: takes an input activation + uses its weights to produce an output activation. The atomic building block of an NN.

concepts.name: gradient
concepts.definition: Partial derivative of the loss with respect to a parameter. Tells the optimizer how to adjust each weight to reduce loss.

concepts.name: loss
concepts.definition: Scalar measure of how badly the network is doing on a batch. The training objective: pick weights that minimize loss across the training set.

concepts.name: optimizer
concepts.definition: Strategy for applying gradients to weights — SGD, Adam, RMSprop, etc. Maps (weight, gradient) → updated_weight.

concepts.name: forward_pass
concepts.definition: Compute output from input by walking layers in order. Pure function of inputs and current weights.

concepts.name: backward_pass
concepts.definition: Compute gradients of loss with respect to every weight by reverse-mode autodiff. Output of one pass = input to the optimizer.

concepts.name: embedding
concepts.definition: Learned dense vector representation of a discrete symbol (word, category, ID). The bridge between discrete graph data and continuous tensor space.

concepts.name: softmax
concepts.definition: Map a vector of scores to a probability distribution by exponentiating then normalizing. The standard output transform for classification.

concepts.name: nonlinearity
concepts.definition: A non-affine elementwise activation function (ReLU, GELU, sigmoid, tanh). Without one, stacked linear layers collapse to a single linear layer.

concepts.name: training_loop
concepts.definition: Repeat: sample batch → forward_pass → loss → backward_pass → optimizer step. The procedure that turns random weights into trained weights.

concepts.name: regularization
concepts.definition: Modifications to loss or architecture that restrict parameter complexity (L2, dropout, weight decay). Trades training fit for generalization.

concepts.name: batch
concepts.definition: A set of inputs processed together in one forward+backward pass. Trades memory for gradient-noise reduction.

patterns.name: linear_layer
patterns.definition: Affine transformation y = Wx + b with learnable weight matrix W and bias b. The fundamental parametric layer.
patterns.mechanism: Allocate weight tensor [out_dim, in_dim] + bias [out_dim]; forward = matmul + add; gradients reach W and b via the chain rule.
patterns.tradeoff: Pure linear has no representational depth — needs nonlinearities between stacked linears to be more than a single matrix.

patterns.name: relu_activation
patterns.definition: Elementwise max(0, x). The default nonlinearity — cheap, well-behaved gradients, scale-invariant on the positive side.
patterns.mechanism: Apply max(0, .) elementwise on forward; gradient is 1 where input>0, 0 elsewhere.
patterns.tradeoff: Dead neurons: units stuck at negative input never recover. GELU/LeakyReLU mitigate.

patterns.name: gelu_activation
patterns.definition: Gaussian Error Linear Unit: x * Phi(x). Smoother than ReLU, the standard nonlinearity in Transformer-style networks.
patterns.mechanism: Apply x * 0.5 * (1 + erf(x/sqrt(2))) elementwise; or the tanh approximation for speed.
patterns.tradeoff: Slightly more expensive than ReLU; pays off when smooth gradients matter (deep attention stacks).

patterns.name: embedding_table
patterns.definition: Lookup table that maps each integer ID in [0, vocab_size) to a learned dense vector. The standard way to feed discrete symbols into an NN.
patterns.mechanism: Allocate matrix [vocab_size, embed_dim]; forward = gather rows by ID; gradients accumulate into rows that were used.
patterns.tradeoff: Memory grows with vocab_size; cold-start: rows for unseen IDs are random until trained.

patterns.name: softmax_classifier
patterns.definition: Linear projection to n_classes followed by softmax to produce a probability over classes. The standard top of any classification network.
patterns.mechanism: linear_layer to [n_classes]; softmax produces P(class | input); pairs with cross_entropy_loss.
patterns.tradeoff: Assumes mutually exclusive classes; for multi-label use n independent sigmoids instead.

patterns.name: mlp_block
patterns.definition: Stacked linear layers with nonlinearities between them — linear, relu, linear. The general-purpose function approximator.
patterns.mechanism: Compose 2-3 linear_layers separated by relu_activation; output dim matches the downstream task (softmax_classifier for classification, single scalar for regression).
patterns.tradeoff: No structural prior — needs more data than architecturally informed alternatives (CNN for grids, Transformer for sequences).

patterns.name: gradient_descent
patterns.definition: Update each weight by w := w - lr * grad. The simplest optimizer; the baseline against which Adam etc. are improvements.
patterns.mechanism: After backward_pass, walk the parameter list and apply the per-weight update.
patterns.tradeoff: Slow convergence on ill-conditioned losses; sensitive to learning_rate choice.

patterns.name: adam_optimizer
patterns.definition: Adaptive moment estimation — per-weight running mean + variance of gradients, scales the update by both. The default optimizer for most modern NNs.
patterns.mechanism: Per weight: m = beta1*m + (1-beta1)*g; v = beta2*v + (1-beta2)*g**2; w := w - lr * m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps).
patterns.tradeoff: 3x memory of pure SGD (stores m, v per weight); harder to reason about convergence formally.

patterns.name: cross_entropy_loss
patterns.definition: -sum(target_i * log(predicted_i)) over classes. The standard classification loss; equivalent to negative log-likelihood under a categorical model.
patterns.mechanism: Pair with softmax_classifier; gradient w.r.t. logits is just (predicted - target) — numerically clean.
patterns.tradeoff: Requires probabilities; needs label smoothing for overconfident predictions.

patterns.name: mse_loss
patterns.definition: Mean squared error: mean((predicted - target)**2). The standard regression loss; gradient is just (predicted - target).
patterns.mechanism: Compute (predicted - target)**2 elementwise; mean reduces to a scalar.
patterns.tradeoff: Sensitive to outliers; for heavy-tailed targets use mean absolute error or Huber.

patterns.name: residual_connection
patterns.definition: Add the layer's input to its output: y = f(x) + x. Lets gradient flow past the layer unchanged, enabling much deeper networks.
patterns.mechanism: After computing f(x), add x (with matching shape) to produce final output.
patterns.tradeoff: Requires shape match between input and output; needs a 1x1 projection if dims differ.

patterns.name: layer_normalization
patterns.definition: Normalize each sample's activations to zero mean unit variance over the feature dim. Stabilizes training in deep networks, especially Transformers.
patterns.mechanism: Per sample: y = gamma * (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps) + beta; learnable gamma, beta restore representational capacity.
patterns.tradeoff: Adds compute and two learnable tensors per layer; rarely needed in shallow networks.

patterns.name: attention_block
patterns.definition: Softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V — every position attends to every other position weighted by content similarity. The kernel of Transformer architectures.
patterns.mechanism: Linear projections to Q, K, V from the same input; scaled dot-product attention; output is a weighted sum of V rows.
patterns.tradeoff: O(n^2) in sequence length; multi-head and flash-attention mitigate.

patterns.name: convolutional_kernel
patterns.definition: Apply a small weight tensor by sliding it across a spatial input — local connectivity + weight sharing.
patterns.mechanism: Allocate kernel [out_ch, in_ch, kh, kw]; convolve with input; bias per output channel.
patterns.tradeoff: Assumes locality + translation invariance; bad fit for non-spatial data.

targets.notes: FSDD plateaued at 44.4% with the Bernoulli-KL recogniser. 5 acoustic features (voicing, sibilant, sonorant, formant_present, noise_burst) → 10 digit classes. An MLP head over the same band-mean signature is the natural next move; the cortex should pick softmax_classifier or mlp_block here.
Given a query subgraph and a candidate, produce a similarity scalar. Pure recogniser-style soft scoring — fits attention_block over node embeddings.
Map a Concept node (by ID) to a fixed-dim dense vector. embedding_table is the textbook fit; an mlp_block over the Concept's attribute vector is the alternative when the table is too sparse.

Constructible target — |x| is exactly representable by a 2-hidden-unit ReLU net (§2.1 of net_construction_techniques.md). The cortex should pick `abs_gadget` and render the weights directly from the gadget's matrices; NO training.
Constructible target — max(x, y) = ReLU(x − y) + y. Cortex picks `max_gadget` and renders the weights directly.
Constructible compositional target — the cortex picks `max_abs_2d_gadget`, the assembler chains abs_2d_gadget then max_gadget, and construct_weights renders both sub-gadgets' matrices in order.

First smooth (non-exact-CPWL) constructible target — the cortex picks `square_pwl_signed_gadget` which approximates x² via abs then a 10-segment PWL. Error ≤ 0.25%. Gateway to polarization multiplication (§2.4): x·y = ½·((x+y)² − x² − y²).

First MULTIPLICATION target — constructed from §2.1 abs + §2.3 PWL square via §2.4 polarization. The cortex picks `polarization_multiply_gadget` which chains [polarization_inputs → abs_3d → square_pwl_10_3d → polarization_combine]. Restricted to [−0.5, 0.5]² so x+y stays in [−1, 1] where square_pwl is valid. Unlocks monomials and polynomials.

First MONOMIAL target. Built on heterogeneous-parallel: lift [x] → [x, x²] using cpwl_broadcast then cpwl_heteroparallel, then multiply via the polarization gadget. cube_gadget chain is monomial_lift_x_x2_gadget → polarization_multiply_gadget. Six layers total. Unlocks x⁴ via x·x³, x⁵ via x²·x³, and polynomials by linear combinations.
